questions.question: Which of the following rocks is formed when the molten magma cools down and becomes solid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Igneous Rock.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Igneous rock, or magmatic rock,** is one of the three main rock types, the others being sedimentary and **metamorphic.**
 
• Igneous rock is formed through the **cooling and solidification of magma or lava.**
 
• The magma can be derived from partial melts of existing rocks in either a planet's **mantle or crust.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__ **

 
 

 **Metamorphic Rocks**
 
 
 
• Metamorphic rocks started out as some other type of rock, but have been substantially changed from their original i**gneous, sedimentary, or earlier metamorphic form.**
 
• Metamorphic rocks form when rocks are subjected to high **heat, high pressure, hot mineral-rich fluids, **or, more commonly, some combination of these factors.
 
 
 
 

 **Sedimentary Rocks**
 
 
 
• Sedimentary rocks are types of rock that are formed by the accumulation or **deposition of mineral or organic particles** at the Earth's surface, followed by cementation. Sedimentation is the collective name for processes that cause these particles to** settle in place.**
 
 
 
 

 **Sandstone**
 
 
 
• Sandstone is a clastic sedimentary** rock composed mainly of sand-sized** (0.0625 to 2 mm) silicate grains. Sandstones comprise about 20–25% of all sedimentary rocks.

questions.question: Which government launched the 'Pirul Lao-Paise Pao' campaign to mitigate forest fires by incentivizing the collection of Pine leaves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand Government**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami** initiated the **"Pirul Lao-Paise Pao"** Mission in **Rudraprayag **district to address the forest fire situation prevalent across the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

questions.question: Nagauri Ashwagandha, which recently received the GI tag, is known for its distinct characteristics due to agro-climatic conditions of Nagaur district. Which of the following statements related to Nagauri Ashwagandha is NOT correct?

options.text: It is cultivated in the arid and semi-arid regions of Nagaur district in Rajasthan
It is valued for its medicinal properties and use in Ayurveda
The GI tag grants a patent-like exclusive ownership to individual farmers
The GI tag provides legal protection to the product’s geographical identity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the GI tag grants a patent-like exclusive ownership to individual farmers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nagauri Ashwagandha is cultivated in the arid and semi-arid regions of Nagaur district in Rajasthan. These regions have unique agro-climatic conditions that contribute to the distinct characteristics of Nagauri Ashwagandha. ***Hence, the statement 1 is correct**.*
 
• Nagauri Ashwagandha is highly valued for its medicinal properties and its widespread use in Ayurveda. It is used in various herbal medicines to improve immunity, vitality, and overall health. ***Hence, the statement 2 is correct**.*
 
• The GI tag does not grant a patent-like exclusive ownership to individual farmers. Instead, the GI tag provides collective rights to all producers within the geographical region. ***Hence, the statement 3 is incorrect***.
 
• The GI tag provides legal protection to the product’s geographical identity. This ensures that only those registered under the GI tag can use the name "Nagauri Ashwagandha" for selling the product, protecting its authenticity and heritage. ***Hence, the statement 4 is correct**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geographical Indication (GI) Tag:**

 
 
• A **Geographical Indication (GI)** tag is a certification provided to products that have a specific geographical origin and possess qualities or reputation due to that origin.
 
• It is governed under the **Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999** in India.
 
• Examples of GI-tagged products include **Darjeeling Tea**, **Kashmiri Saffron**, and **Mysore Silk.**
 
 
 
• **Nagauri Ashwagandha:**
 
 
• **Nagauri Ashwagandha** is a medicinal plant grown in the Nagaur district of Rajasthan.
 
• It is known for its high potency and purity due to the unique agro-climatic conditions of the region.
 
• It has applications in **Ayurveda** for enhancing immunity, reducing stress, and improving vitality.
 
 
 
• **Importance of GI Tags:**
 
 
• GI tags promote the economic prosperity of producers by enhancing the marketability of their products.
 
• They ensure authenticity, prevent misuse of product names, and foster heritage preservation.
 
• GI-tagged products often attract higher demand and premium pricing in national and international markets.
 
 
 
• **Key Legal Framework:**
 
 
• GI tags are valid for **10 years** and can be renewed indefinitely.
 
• Producers within the registered geographical region are collectively entitled to use the GI tag.
 
• Misuse or unauthorized use of GI-tagged names can lead to legal consequences under the **GI Act**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference Between GI Tag and Patent:**

 
 
• A **GI tag** provides collective rights based on geographical origin, while a patent grants exclusive rights to inventors for innovations.
 
• GI tags are region-specific, and multiple producers can use them, whereas patents are granted to individuals or organizations.
 
• GI tags are primarily used for agricultural, handicraft, and industrial products, while patents focus on inventions and technological advancements.
 
 
 
• **Example of GI-tagged Medicinal Products:**
 
 
• **Neem** and **Turmeric** are examples of Indian medicinal plants with significant market value due to their therapeutic properties.
 
• They are widely used in **Ayurvedic medicines** and have gained recognition globally for their healing potential.

questions.question: Champaran Satyagraha took place in which of the states of India as first experiment of Mahatma Gandhi after his return to India from South Africa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Champaran Satyagraha** of **1917** was the first **Satyagraha** movement inspired by **Mahatma Gandhi** and a major revolt in the **Indian Independence Movement**.

• It took place in the **Champaran district** of **Bihar**, where farmers were forced by **British planters** to grow **Indigo** under extremely oppressive conditions.

• The movement was primarily directed against the **Tinkathia system**, which legally compelled tenant farmers to plant indigo on **3/20th** of their total land holding.

• **Raj Kumar Shukla**, a local peasant leader, traveled to meet **Gandhi** and persistently requested him to visit **Bihar** to address the grievances of the **indigo cultivators**.

• This movement marked the first time **Mahatma Gandhi** used the tool of **Civil Disobedience** in India, leading to his arrest and subsequent release after mass protests.

• Following the agitation, the **Champaran Agrarian Committee** was formed with **Mahatma Gandhi** as one of its members to investigate the condition of the peasants.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Mahatma Gandhi's Early Activism**:

• Gandhi returned to India from **South Africa** on **January 9, 1915**. This date is now commemorated as **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas**.

• Before **Champaran**, he spent a year traveling across **British India** on the advice of **Gopal Krishna Gokhale** to understand the political and social climate.

• **Legislative Impact**:

• The struggle resulted in the passage of the **Champaran Agrarian Act** in **1918**, which abolished the **Tinkathia system** and refunded part of the illegal dues collected from the farmers.

• **Associated Leaders**:

• The movement saw the emergence of future national leaders such as **Dr. Rajendra Prasad**, **Anugrah Narayan Sinha**, **Mazhar-ul-Haq**, **Mahadev Desai**, and **J.B. Kripalani**.

• **Subsequent Satyagrahas**:

• Following the success in **Bihar**, Gandhi led the **Ahmedabad Mill Strike** (his first hunger strike) and the **Kheda Satyagraha** (his first non-cooperation movement) in **1918**.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Inter-State Council is a constitutional body under Article 263.

2. Its recommendations are binding on the Union and States.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Inter-State Council** is a constitutional body established under Article 263 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It was created to facilitate coordination between the Union and State governments on matters of national importance.
 
• The council is primarily an advisory body and its recommendations are **not binding** on the Union or State governments.
 
• It consists of the Prime Minister as the Chairman, Chief Ministers of all States, Union Ministers, and other members as decided by the President.
 
• The council's primary function is to investigate and discuss subjects where coordination is required between the Union and States.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background of Article 263:**

 
 
• Article 263 empowers the President of India to establish an Inter-State Council if it appears necessary for better coordination between the Union and State governments.
 
• The primary roles include:
 
 
• Inquiring into disputes between states.
 
• Discussing subjects of common interest.
 
• Making recommendations for policy formulation and implementation.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Historical Development:**
 
 
• The Inter-State Council was established in 1990 by a Presidential Order following the recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission.
 
• The Sarkaria Commission emphasized the need for a constitutional mechanism to address Union-State relations more effectively.

questions.question:
With reference to the religious geography of Jammu and Kashmir, consider the following statements:

Statement I: The Mantalai temple houses a shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva known as Aparneswar and features a sacred pond.

Statement II: Goddess Parvati is believed to have been born at Mantalai and used to bathe at the nearby Gauri Kund.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both Statement I and Statement II are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mantalai Temple**:

 
 
• **Statement I**: The Mantalai temple indeed houses a shrine dedicated to **Lord Shiva**, known as **Aparneswar**. It features a **sacred pond**, which is of great religious significance to devotees. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Goddess Parvati’s Connection**:
 
 
• **Statement II**: According to Hindu mythology, **Goddess Parvati** is believed to have been born at **Mantalai**. The **Gauri Kund**, located nearby, is considered the place where she used to bathe. This connection enhances the spiritual importance of the site. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• The location is situated in the **Udhampur District** of Jammu and Kashmir and is an essential site for **Hindu devotees**.
 
• The temple and the associated mythological sites are also significant for **pilgrimage tourism**, attracting visitors from across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Religious Significance of Mantalai**:

 
 
• Mantalai is a sacred location associated with the **marriage of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati**, as per Hindu scriptures.
 
• The site has mythological importance and is mentioned in several ancient **Puranas**.
 
 
 
• **Gauri Kund**:
 
 
• Located near Mantalai, **Gauri Kund** is a small natural water body considered sacred by devotees.
 
• The Kund is named after **Goddess Parvati**, who is also known as Gauri.
 
 
 
• **Tourism Potential**:
 
 
• The region is a popular destination for **pilgrimage tourism**, attracting both devotees and tourists interested in the cultural and spiritual heritage of India.
 
• Efforts are being made to promote the site under **Jammu and Kashmir’s tourism development programs**.
 
 
 
• **Other Religious Sites in Jammu and Kashmir**:
 
 
• **Vaishno Devi Temple**: One of the most famous pilgrimage sites dedicated to Goddess Durga.
 
• **Amarnath Cave**: A sacred cave shrine dedicated to Lord Shiva, known for its naturally occurring ice Shiva Linga.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hindu Mythology**: The region of Jammu and Kashmir is rich in sites associated with Hindu mythology, making it a significant area for religious studies and pilgrimages.
 
• **Preservation Efforts**: Both the central and state governments have been working to preserve the cultural and religious heritage of Mantalai and similar sites.
 
• **Historical and Archaeological Value**: Mantalai and its surrounding areas also hold archaeological significance, with ancient structures and artifacts linked to the **Shaivite tradition**.

questions.question: Which festival in Kerala is closely associated with boat races and the celebration of the new paddy harvest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Onam**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Onam** is the official **state festival of Kerala**, observed during the month of **Chingam** (August–September), which marks the beginning of the **Malayalam calendar**.

• It is primarily a **harvest festival** that celebrates the bounty of nature and commemorates the annual visit of the legendary **Asura King Mahabali** from the underworld to see his subjects.

• The festival is globally renowned for the **Vallam Kali** or snake boat races, particularly the **Nehru Trophy Boat Race** held on the **Punnamada Lake** in **Alappuzha**, where long boats rowed by hundreds of oarsmen compete.

• Key cultural elements include the preparation of **Pookalam** (intricate floral carpets), the **Onasadya** (a grand vegetarian feast served on banana leaves), and traditional performing arts such as **Pulikali** (tiger dance) and **Kummattikali**.

• The festivities span **ten days**, beginning with **Atham** and culminating in the most important day, **Thiruvonam**, symbolizing prosperity, equality, and communal harmony.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Attukal Pongala**:

• This is a major female-centric festival held at the **Attukal Bhagavathy Temple** in **Thiruvananthapuram**.

• It holds the **Guinness World Record** for being the largest annual religious gathering of women, where devotees prepare a sweet offering of **Pongala** (rice, jaggery, and coconut) in earthen pots.

• **Thrissur Pooram**:

• Considered the mother of all poorams, it is held at the **Vadakkunnathan Temple** in **Thrissur** during the Malayalam month of **Medam**.

• It was conceptualized by **Sakthan Thampuran**, the Maharaja of Cochin, and is famous for its competitive display of **caparisoned elephants** and **Ilanjithara Melam** (percussion ensemble).

• **Vishu**:

• This festival marks the **Malayalam New Year** and usually falls in the month of April, signifying the **Spring Equinox**.

• The most important ritual is the **Vishu Kani**, an arrangement of auspicious items like **Kanikkonna** (golden shower flowers) and coins, which is the first thing people see upon waking.

questions.question: Who among the following is the first man (after Bjorn Borg in 1980) to win the French Open and Wimbledon Singles Title back to back?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rafael Nadal**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• In **2008**, the Spanish tennis legend **Rafael Nadal** achieved the rare feat of winning the **French Open** and **Wimbledon** singles titles back-to-back in the same calendar year.

• This accomplishment made him the first man to complete the **Channel Slam** since the Swedish player **Bjorn Borg**, who successfully managed the transition three times between **1978 and 1980**.

• Nadal dominance on the **clay courts** of **Roland Garros** culminated in his fourth consecutive title in June **2008**, where he defeated **Roger Federer** in the final.

• Just weeks later, Nadal defeated Federer again in the **2008 Wimbledon final**, a historic match lasting 4 hours and 48 minutes, widely considered the **greatest tennis match** ever played.

• The **Channel Slam** is considered one of the most difficult challenges in professional tennis due to the extreme difference in ball bounce and speed between **clay** and **grass** surfaces.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Roger Federer**:

• Federer became the next player to achieve this feat in **2009**, winning the **French Open** to complete his **Career Grand Slam** and then winning **Wimbledon** shortly after.

• **John McEnroe**:

• A former world number one known for his **grass-court** prowess; however, he never won a singles title at the **French Open**, famously losing the 1984 final to Ivan Lendl.

• **Daniel Nestor**:

• A prolific **Canadian doubles specialist** who completed the **Career Golden Slam** in doubles but did not compete at the same elite level in **Grand Slam singles**.

• **Channel Slam Context**:

• Since Nadal in 2008, other players to achieve the back-to-back **French Open-Wimbledon** titles include **Novak Djokovic** (2021) and **Carlos Alcaraz** (2024).

</ul

questions.question:

questions.question: Which of the following events led Mahatma Gandhi to suspend the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1922?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Chauri Chaura incident**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Non-Cooperation Movement** was a significant phase of the Indian independence struggle, launched by **Mahatma Gandhi** in **1920** following the **Nagpur session** of the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• On **February 4, 1922**, a violent clash occurred at **Chauri Chaura**, a village in the **Gorakhpur district** of the **United Provinces** (modern-day Uttar Pradesh).
 
• During a procession of volunteers, the local police opened fire on the crowd; in retaliation, the enraged demonstrators set the **police station** ablaze, leading to the death of **22 to 23 policemen**.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, an advocate of **Ahimsa (non-violence)**, was devastated by the violence and believed that the Indian masses were not yet sufficiently trained for a disciplined **Satyagraha**.
 
• As a result, Gandhi undertook a **five-day fast** as penance and convinced the **Congress Working Committee** to pass the **Bardoli Resolution** on **February 12, 1922**, which officially **suspended** the movement nationwide.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre**:
 
 
• This occurred on **April 13, 1919**, in **Amritsar**, where **General Dyer** ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering.
 
• This event was one of the primary reasons for the **commencement** of the movement, not its end.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act Protests**:
 
 
• The **Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919**, known as the **Rowlatt Act**, allowed the British to detain political prisoners without trial.
 
• The **Rowlatt Satyagraha** was the first pan-India political campaign organized by **Gandhi** against this 'Black Act'.
 
 
 
• **Khilafat Conference Decision**:
 
 
• The **Khilafat Movement**, led by **Shaukat Ali** and **Mohammad Ali**, aimed to protect the **Caliphate** in **Turkey**.
 
• Gandhi aligned the **Non-Cooperation Movement** with the Khilafat cause to strengthen **Hindu-Muslim unity** against British rule.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Match the 'Temple' with its 'Location':

 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 Temple
 Location
 
 

 (i) Sas-Bahu Temple
 (a) Abhaneri
 
 

 (ii) Harshat Mata Temple
 (b) Nagda
 
 

 (iii) Kiradu Temple
 (c) Osian
 
 

 (iv) Sachiya Mata Temple
 (d) Barmer
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i)-b, (ii)-a, (iii)-d, (iv)-c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sas-Bahu Temple**: This historic temple is located in **Nagda**, which was the first capital of the **Mewar Kingdom**, near **Udaipur**. The name is a corruption of "**Sahastra-Bahu**," meaning "one with a thousand arms," referring to **Lord Vishnu**. ***Hence, match (i)-b is correct.***
 
• **Harshat Mata Temple**: This temple is situated in **Abhaneri** village in the **Dausa** district of **Rajasthan**. It is located right next to the famous **Chand Baori** stepwell and is dedicated to **Goddess Harshat Mata**, the goddess of happiness and joy. ***Hence, match (ii)-a is correct.***
 
• **Kiradu Temple**: Located in the **Thar Desert**, approximately **35 km** from **Barmer**, these temples are a group of five structures known for their intricate carvings. They are often referred to as the "**Khajuraho of Rajasthan**" due to their **Solanki style** of architecture. ***Hence, match (iii)-d is correct.***
 
• **Sachiya Mata Temple**: This temple is located in **Osian** (near **Jodhpur**) and is an important pilgrimage site for the **Oswal Jain** community. It was built by the **Parmar King Upendre** for his tutelary deity. ***Hence, match (iv)-c is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sas-Bahu Temple (Nagda)**:

 
 
• Built in the **10th Century**, it consists of two temples of different sizes. The larger one (Sas) is surrounded by **ten subsidiary shrines**, while the smaller one (Bahu) has **four**.
 
• It displays the **Maha-Maru** style of architecture, featuring complex carvings on the **lintels** and **pillars** depicting scenes from the **Ramayana**.
 
 
 
• **Harshat Mata Temple (Abhaneri)**:
 
 
• Originally built in the **8th-9th Century** during the reign of the **Chahamana dynasty** (likely under **King Chand**).
 
• Though largely in ruins now due to **Islamic invasions** in the **11th Century**, the remaining fragments showcase the high level of **Indian sculptural art** from the **early medieval period**.
 
 
 
• **Kiradu Temples (Barmer)**:
 
 
• The group consists of five temples, of which the **Someshvara temple** is the most remarkable and well-preserved.
 
• They were built between the **11th and 12th Centuries**. The architecture is characterized by the **Maru-Gurjara** style, with highly decorative **Shikharas** and **base moldings**.
 
 
 
• **Sachiya Mata Temple (Osian)**:
 
 
• **Osian** is known as the "**Khajuraho of Marwar**" due to its cluster of **Brahmanical and Jain temples** dating from the **8th to 12th Centuries**.
 
• The temple complex is situated on a hill and features a series of **beautifully carved arches** (Toranas) and **sculptures** of various Hindu deities like **Vishnu**, **Shiva**, and **Surya**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Maha-Maru Style**: Most of these temples represent the **Maha-Maru** or **Maru-Gurjara** architectural traditions that flourished in **Western India** (Rajasthan and Gujarat) during the **medieval period**.
 
• **Preservation**: Many of these sites are under the protection of the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)** due to their historical and cultural significance in representing the evolution of **temple architecture** in **North India**.
 
• **Cultural Synthesis**: Sites like **Osian** demonstrate a unique **synthesis** of **Vedic and Jain** traditions, where deities of both religions are often found within the same temple vicinity or administrative influence.

questions.question: The Preamble to the Constitution of India was amended by the 42ⁿd Amendment Act and inserted the following words in - the existing Preamble,
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**'Socialist, secular' and 'integrity'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Preamble to the Constitution of India** is the introductory statement that sets forth the objectives and purposes of the Constitution.
 
• **The 42nd Amendment Act **was passed in 1976 during the period of Emergency in India and brought about several changes to the Constitution.
 
• The terms "Socialist", "Secular", and "Integrity" were added to the Preamble of Indian Constitution in 1976 through the 42nd Constitutional Amendment.
 
• However, in 1977, when the Emergency was lifted and a new government came to power, the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were separated by a comma, and the word 'Integrity' was added.
 
• Therefore, the current version of the Preamble reads as follows: "We, the people of India, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic and to secure to all its citizens: Justice, social, economic and political; Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship; Equality of status and of opportunity; and to promote among them all Fraternity assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation."

questions.question: Which major Hindu religious fair held in Uttar Pradesh is internationally famous for the massive pilgrimages that take place at the Triveni Sangam (the confluence of the Ganges, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati rivers)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kumbh Mela**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kumbh Mela** is a massive Hindu pilgrimage and the world's largest peaceful religious gathering, held in **Prayagraj**, **Uttar Pradesh**, every **12 years**.
 
• It takes place at the **Triveni Sangam**, which is the sacred confluence of three rivers: the **Ganges**, the **Yamuna**, and the mythical or invisible **Saraswati**.
 
• The festival follows a **12-year cycle** (Purna Kumbh) and a **6-year cycle** (Ardh Kumbh), with the locations rotating between **Haridwar**, **Ujjain**, **Nashik**, and **Prayagraj** based on astrological alignments of **Jupiter** and the **Sun**.
 
• Historically, the fair was recorded by the Chinese traveler **Hiuen Tsang** in the 7th century during the reign of Emperor **Harshavardhana**.
 
• In **December 2017**, the **UNESCO** Intergovernmental Committee for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage inscribed Kumbh Mela on the **Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deva Mela**
 
 
• Located in **Barabanki**, Uttar Pradesh, this fair is held at the shrine of the Sufi Saint **Haji Waris Ali Shah**.
 
• It is renowned for promoting **communal harmony** and is celebrated during the months of October and November.
 
 
 
• **Pushkar Fair**
 
 
• Held in the state of **Rajasthan**, it is one of the world's largest **camel and livestock fairs**, occurring on the banks of **Pushkar Lake**.
 
• It coincides with the religious festival of **Kartik Purnima** and is famous for its proximity to the rare **Brahma Temple**.
 
 
 
• **Taj Mahotsav**
 
 
• An annual **10-day cultural festival** organized by **Uttar Pradesh Tourism** in **Agra** every **February**.
 
• It showcases India's rich **arts, crafts, and cuisines**, drawing inspiration from the **Mughal era**.
 
 
</ul
